reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be an arbitrary measurable space, K a measurable subset of E, and k0 a chosen element of the subtype K. Define r:E->K by r(x)=x regarded as an element of K when x belongs to K, and r(x)=k0 otherwise. Then r is measurable from E to K with its induced subtype measurable structure. The assumption k0 in K supplies nonemptiness; no topology or compactness is assumed.
objects: Measurable space E, subset K, fallback k0 in K, membership-based map r.
domains: r:E->K, with K the subtype equipped with its induced measurable structure.
quantifiers: For every measurable E, every measurable K and every fallback k0 in K, r is measurable.
assumptions: K measurable; given fallback is an actual point of K.
conclusion: Measurable map r that fixes points of K and returns fallback outside K.
scopes: Pointwise definition for every x in E; measurability is global.
constant_dependencies: r depends on K and fallback; no numerical constants.
context_ambiguities: None identified from the supplied statement and definition context.
